episodes.199527: A cluster of severe thunderstorms crossed the tidal Potomac River into southern Maryland and produced localized damaging wind gusts.
episodes.199532: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms crossed the tidal Potomac River resulting in gale- to storm-force wind gusts. Later that evening, squalls associated with a strong cold front resulted in a rapid onset of gale-force winds.
episodes.199535: Squalls along a strong cold front resulted in a rapid onset of gale conditions overnight.
episodes.199667: With lingering moisture and the Atlantic and Gulf sea breezes, diurnal heating led to shower and thunderstorm development in the afternoon of March 31st. With southwesterly mid-level and surface flow, the best dynamics favored convective development across the metropolitan portion of Palm Beach County.
episodes.199779: A prefrontal trough pushed across Eastern North Carolina during the evening of March thirty-first. As this occurred, isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed with a few of these storms becoming strong in nature. Within the strongest storms, strong wind gusts, frequent lightning and locally enhanced seas occurred. Storms generally impacted the coastal waters south of Cape Lookout during the evening of the thirty-first. This activity quickly weakened overnight.
episodes.199867: Storms advanced ahead of a cold front and an upper low leading to a few low-end severe wind gusts over both land and marine environments.
episodes.200087: A wavy, broken line of prefrontal storms draped across the lower Tennessee Valley and Southeast shifted into and through the Carolinas during the afternoon into the evening. The lead band of storms weakened significantly as it shifted into the southern Piedmont, but discrete thunderstorms ahead of the line moved into the Triangle, initially producing narrow swaths of sub-severe hail and damaging winds, before congealing into a singular bowing segment as it moved into the northern and central Coastal Plain.
episodes.200246: A rainy period over the upper and middle WI River valley and snow melt raised water levels to flood stage at the Wisconsin River at Portage for the early portion of April.
episodes.200572: Storms moving offshore produced strong to severe wind gusts along the Brevard and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.200573: A severe thunderstorm damaged a few mobile homes in Melbourne, south of the Melbourne International Airport.
episodes.200680: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed over the eastern plains of southeast Wyoming and gradually turned severe as they approached the Nebraska border. Large hail and a few wind gusts over 60 mph were recorded.
episodes.200681: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed over the eastern plains of southeast Wyoming and gradually turned severe as they approached the Nebraska border. Large hail and a few wind gusts over 60 mph were recorded.
episodes.201117: An approaching cold front resulting in severe storms across the region on the afternoon and evening of March 31.
episodes.201118: An approaching cold front resulted in severe storms across the region in the afternoon and evening of March 31.
episodes.201119: An approaching cold front brought severe storms to portions of the region.
episodes.201155: A cold front moved from the Appalachian Mountains east across Virginia late on March 31 into early on April 1. Scattered severe storms developed in a line ahead of the front across central and eastern Virginia late on March 31, producing damaging winds.
episodes.201156: A cold front moved from the Appalachian Mountains east across the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore late on March 31 into early on April 1. Isolated severe storms developed in a line ahead of the front across portions of the lower Maryland Eastern Shore late on March 31, producing damaging winds.
episodes.201207: An early spring storm brought heavy mountain snow, rain, gusty winds and thunderstorms to interior northern California at the end of March and carried into the evening of April 1st. Storm total snow of 24 to 44 inches was reported above 5000 feet, from March 31 to April 2. Traffic was held on Interstate 80 between Alta and NV stateline due to heavy snow from approximately 10 AM to 2 PM on April 1st, with US Highway 50 held from Meyers to Echo Summit from 12 PM through 3 PM on April 1st. An EF-0 tornado was confirmed in Stanislaus County as well.
episodes.201268: Flooding caused by rapid snowmelt in March continued through mid-April. The Silvies river rose to 14.76 feet, about half a foot under the record of 15.2 feet, on March 29th. The water levels began to decrease, although the area remained inundated. Another warm period in mid-April allowed for the river level to begin rising again. Reaching a secondary peak of 12.58 feet on April 11th. Water dropped below flood stage on April 15th. Flood impacts were observed through mid-late April.
episodes.201668: A bi-modal (in time) severe weather episode occurred across Oklahoma and western-north Texas from the evening of the 1st into the early morning of the 2nd. An initial bout of activity featured scattered supercell thunderstorms across north-central Oklahoma and the Red River Valley. Persistent low stratus into the afternoon of the 1st led to a narrow warm sector by the early evening, with supercell thunderstorms displaying a slightly elevated character. These thunderstorms produced large hail before weakening quickly. As the main (strong) upper trough spread eastward into the early morning hours, additional thunderstorms developed along an advancing cold front. This linear band of thunderstorms produced only intermittent reports of large hail and wind damage despite a strongly sheared and unstable boundary layer.
episodes.202275: A system brought enough instability to produce scattered showers across the region. A weak funnel cloud from one of the showers was reported to have occur over Kootenai County.
episodes.203174: A verified weak tornado from a individual storm cell on the afternoon of April 1st.

A brief EF-0 tornado touched down at 2 ENE Salida at 2:13 PM PDT and was on the ground for 0.9 miles until 2:15 PM PDT. The tornado moved through several orchards and 3 properties. Dozens of almond trees were uprooted and large tree branches were broken. Minor structure damage observed at the properties included a covered patio and roof material ripped off, a broken window, and outbuilding and metal fencing was displaced, and a large trailer was lifted and moved approximately 20 feet.

The public submitted several photographs of a tornado touched down northwest of the St. Anthony Sand Dunes. It appeared to be a very weak tornado and no damage was found as the tornado was in an open field.
